real_corpus.command: node test/language-python/real-corpus-runner.mjs --root fastapi-full-stack-template=<checkout of fastapi-full-stack-template> --root flask-official-tutorial=<checkout of flask-official-tutorial> --root django-urlpatterns-reverse=<checkout of django-urlpatterns-reverse>
real_corpus.checkout_method: per case, in a temporary directory: git init; git remote add origin https://github.com/<repository>.git; git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 --filter=blob:none origin <commit>; git sparse-checkout set --no-cone <sparse_paths>; git checkout --detach <commit>; HEAD must equal the pinned commit. The runner only parses the selected files; nothing from those repositories is executed.

limits.statement: The shadow scanners read static decorators and literal URL patterns. FastAPI router.add_api_route and the api_route decorator, Flask app.add_url_rule and a MethodView registered with add_url_rule produce neither an endpoint or registration nor an unknown, so an empty result does not mean the application has no such route.

A reported path is the declaring module path, not necessarily the served URL: FastAPI include_router mounts are recorded but the endpoint stays router-local, Flask register_blueprint(url_prefix=...) is ignored and the path keeps the blueprint prefix, and a Django include((module, namespace)) is an explicit unknown while the child module pattern is still reported without the outer prefix.

Computed prefixes, methods and patterns, comprehensions, lambdas, f-strings, star imports, conditionally imported names, import cycles, urlpatterns mutation and several annotation forms are reported as unknown or the scanner abstains. Nothing is evaluated, so none of these results is a support claim; for a star import and a conditional import no reason is reported.
A @dataclass produces no model fact and no diagnostic, and a pydantic v2 model_config assignment is reported as a field while the validator is not seen.

A match statement is a PYTHON_SYNTAX_ERROR on line 1 under Python 3.9.6 and parses under 3.11, 3.12 and 3.14, so what the analyzer can read depends on the interpreter that runs the helper. No fixture uses it.

The syntax-error message and columns, the runtime block and the message of an over-buffer failure differ by interpreter version or path, so the pinned outputs leave them out and pin the error code (and, for a syntax error, the line) only.

The corpus manifest lists reserved holdouts that belong to another track. This record holds no checkout of them; the runner only echoes their id, repository, commit and owner, so nothing is recorded for them.
Only the selected files of the three pinned public repositories were run. Other repositories, other files of those repositories and any performance or scale figure are not recorded.

python-package-boundary runs npm pack and npm install of the packed repository root with a 15 second timeout per npm call, so the root package.json is an external input of the result. Network access was available in every recorded run; behaviour without access to the npm registry was not observed.
The CI run on the push of the base commit ended with conclusion cancelled, so no CI result is recorded for it.

The recorded outputs, hashes and counts were generated on one machine (macOS arm64) with Node 24 and Python 3.14.8 as the default interpreter. The fixture outputs and the corpus stdout hash were also compared under Python 3.9.6, 3.11.15 and 3.12.13; other operating systems and architectures were not observed.

verification.recomputed: bytes, git_blob_sha1 and sha256 of every pinned file, per-file and total test counts, the exit code and counts of both commands, the first runner line, every fixture output hash and every expected value, and the recorded corpus report (against its stdout hash, its byte count and the manifest at the base commit) are recomputed by baseline-record.test.mjs and never read back from the record.
levels: always: the record is well formed and any edit that is not re-sealed is reported, because artifact_digest is a SHA-256 over the canonical serialization of the whole record except its own value (fixture calls, expected values, classes and origins, limit statements, statuses and fixture lists, hashes, sizes, counts, exit codes, commit ids and every other field)

live files: size, sha256 and blob id are recomputed from the checkout; a file that disagrees in one hash or in size alone is damage and fails; a file that matches neither hash is drift, which skips the live replays while the pinned commit decides

pinned commit: the base commit is fetched once when absent and the sizes and digests of all pinned files, the runner included, are recomputed from its own blobs; if the commit is unavailable the test fails, and only BASELINE_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED=1 turns that into an explicit skip
ancestry: a shallow checkout is deepened with git fetch --no-tags --unshallow origin and the base commit must be an ancestor of HEAD

commands: both recorded commands are re-run in an extracted copy of the base commit and must reproduce exit code, counts, per-file counts and every fixture output; they need a Python interpreter (its absence fails, and only BASELINE_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED=1 turns that into an explicit skip) and the npm registry
corpus: the recorded report must equal the report the manifest at the pinned commit allows, hash to the recorded stdout and match its byte count
not_recomputed: real_corpus replay: fetching the three pinned commits and running the runner again is opt-in (BASELINE_CORPUS_FETCH=1) and needs the network; by default the checkouts, command and report are checked against the manifest, the recorded hash and the byte count only, and the sizeBytes of the selected files exist only in the recorded report (the manifest does not carry them), so a consistent edit of a size together with the hash and byte count is caught only by the replay
interpreters_compared and environment: observed once on the generating machine

artifact_digest: tamper evidence, not proof. An edit that is not re-sealed is reported, but whoever edits and re-seals passes it, so the recomputations above are the independent check. Fixture output hashes are recomputed from the calls; limit statements, limit fixture lists, fixture classes and origins are prose that nothing derives from the code and that only the digest binds; a swap between two calls whose outputs are identical is invisible to the replay and is caught only by the digest
